already_extracted_claims: The source states it is important to align with your demographic, citing Boom as a pro-age brand targeting an older demographic.
The source describes a mega menu test where adding a bestsellers carousel, icons, social proof, and moving non-money links to the bottom increased incremental monthly revenue.
The source surveyed Boom's customers and used the results to form PDP updates.

The source describes PDP updates based on customer survey: adding reviews and social proof higher, visible savings, sticky add to cart, gallery thumbnails for usability, and making the guarantee prominent.
The source states that for an older demographic concerned about money-back guarantee, making the guarantee information readily available by the call to action led to more purchases and revenue.
The source advises optimizing the image carousel as a mini landing page with images, testimonials, benefits, UGC, video, and seals, and using actual thumbnails instead of radial dots.
The source asserts more people will scroll through the image carousel in entirety than will go through the whole page.
The source recommends removing the discount box on cart or coupon page if there are no active discounts, because it creates a horrible buying experience.
The source warns that when people see a discount box, they search for coupons, encounter a horrible experience with popups, and often leave the site without buying.
The source added a trust policy bar in the cart highlighting easy returns, support, satisfaction guarantee, and money back guarantee to reassure customers and push them down the funnel.
The source added labels like bestsellers and new to collection pages and advises not adding labels to every product, but ensuring a couple stand out where products are side by side.

The source pulled the price point onto the collection page buttons because Boom's makeup is a consumable repeat-purchase product, reducing steps to add to cart; the source notes it does not work with every product or niche.
The source states mobile collection pages need to show 2x2 and four products above the fold, and that huge hero sections with banners and big text blocks that hide products mean start again.
The source states collection pages should remove decision-making and decision paralysis and instead push people toward best sellers, new products, low in stock, and trending products.

The source redesigned landing pages for Boom's older demographic with listicle style, demographic-matched images, larger fonts, scannable text, clear value-driven headline, bullet points, bolded headlines, and a simple benefit-driven buy box, which performed well on cold traffic.
The source states collection pages should do two things: showcase your product and let people filter easily through your product.
